summary: Takes the user to another page, section or site. Underlined in running text so it is never identified by color alone.
whenToUse: Navigation: another page, a section of this page, an external resource.
Inline in sentences (inline variant), or on its own under a card or a table (standalone).
external for other sites: it opens a new tab and says so.
whenNotToUse: Actions on this screen (save, delete, open a dialog): use Button.
Navigation that should look like a button (a single call to action): use Button with render={<a href />}.

dos.title: Link text says where it goes
dos.text: Screen reader users jump between links out of context: "Read the token guidelines" works alone, "here" does not.

donts.title: "Click here" or a bare URL
donts.text: Both say nothing about the destination.

accessibility: Native <a href>: Enter follows it, it is announced as a link, Cmd or Ctrl+click opens a new tab.
Inline links are underlined (WCAG 1.4.1): color is never the only cue inside text.
external adds target=_blank, rel=noopener noreferrer, an icon and "(opens in a new tab)" for screen readers.
Focus ring hugs the text with a 1px offset so it does not overlap neighbouring lines.
contentGuidelines: Describe the destination, not the action of clicking.
Keep it short: three to six words is ideal.
Do not end link text with punctuation or an arrow glyph.
